subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up — next steps and network contacts
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + Private VPC next steps

Hi Amal — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of your requirements (as I captured them):
- Primary requirement: Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC) in AWS for production inference.
- Preferred connectivity: AWS PrivateLink (preferred) or VPC peering as fallback.
- Control-plane access: IP allowlist for the private control-plane endpoint and audit log delivery.
- Compliance: SOC2 requirement for isolated network segments + dedicated routing.
- Timeline: goal to pilot in May and production by end of June if network approvals go smoothly.

Options we discussed:
1) Hosted API — not acceptable for production due to data isolation needs.
2) Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) — good for predictable throughput; still requires private connectivity if you want isolation from other tenants.
3) Private VPC (what you want) — customer VPC connected to Redwood via PrivateLink or VPC peering; we can offer a private control-plane endpoint plus optional dedicated GPUs if desired.

Technical asks we need from your side to move forward:
- Confirm AWS account ID(s) and VPC CIDR(s) to accept (we can provide a template).
- Preferred connectivity method: PrivateLink (NLB + VPC endpoint) or VPC peering?
- Network contact to set up a 30-min sync (we need someone who can share route table / security group constraints).
- Any IP ranges for egress allowlist (if you require outbound restrictions).

Attached is our latest Redwood VPC checklist (redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf) for your network team — it lists required ports, recommended CIDR sizes, and options for logging and NAT.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please introduce your network engineer (Alex?) on this thread.
2) Sean to propose a 30-min network sync with Alex to walk the checklist.
3) We’ll prepare a draft network diagram and a short runbook for the pilot.
4) If you prefer, we can also scope Dedicated capacity pricing for an initial commit to size GPUs.

Let me know if I missed anything. Available Thursday or Friday this week for the sync.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming FinRetail's interest in the Private VPC option. A few specifics from our side: 

- Cloud: AWS (us-west-2).
- Connectivity preference: PrivateLink first; we prefer endpoint-based connectivity vs peering.
- Control plane: yes, we'll want an allowlist for the control plane IP(s) and strong mutual TLS on the control-channel.

- Timeline: network approvals could take 2-3 weeks once we kick off the network sync.

Hi Amal / Alex — Sean from Redwood's Solutions Engineering team. Thanks for the intro, Amal. I took a quick look at the sketch and wanted to clarify a few technical points before our sync: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering\- PrivateLink (NLB + interface endpoint) is generally our recommended path for customer-managed VPCs because it avoids transitive routing concerns and gives you per-endpoint security controls. Peering works but requires route table management and careful handling of overlapping CIDRs.

2) Control plane allowlist\- We can provide a short list of control-plane IPs to allowlist; additionally we support mTLS on the control channel. If you need a strictly zero-external-egress policy from your subnet hosting inference, we can accommodate with NAT/NLB placement, but that affects how logs/metrics are shipped.

3) Ports and protocols\- Minimum requirements:
   - TCP 443 outbound to our PrivateLink endpoint
   - TCP 22 (optional) only for troubleshooting if you request support access (we can minimize this with just-in-time access)
   - UDP not required for inference traffic

4) IP ranges\- If you can share the VPC CIDR(s) (e.g., 10.10.0.0/16) we’ll validate overlap and recommend subnets for the endpoint and workload. We also need the AWS account ID for endpoint/resource policy.

5) Logging and monitoring\- We can deliver audit logs to your S3 bucket or set up a cross-account bucket for logs; CloudWatch metrics can be shared via cross-account roles.

Proposed short-term plan:
- 30-min network sync: please propose 2 x 30-min slots — I’ll block one and include our network runbook.
- I will attach an updated checklist (network-checklist-v2.pdf) with exact example CloudFormation snippets for PrivateLink/NLB and an example endpoint policy.

Suggested times (PDT): Thu 2027-04-22 09:00-09:30 or Thu 2027-04-22 13:00-13:30. If those don’t work, share Alex’s availability.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.
